I upgraded the dependencies behind the reachable findings, and a fresh `security_scan` now reports 0 findings. The build and the backend tests pass, except for the 19 MQTT tests that need Docker, which isn't available here. I did not run `recon_qa` or the end-to-end tests.

**Dependency changes**

| Package | Change |
|---|---|
| `jsonata` | 2.2.x |
| `protobufjs` | 7.6.x |
| `mysql2` | 3.23.x |
| `liquidjs` | 10.27.x |
| `@grpc/grpc-js` | 1.13.x |
| `ws` | 8.21.x |
| `qs` | 6.16.x |
| `vue-i18n` | 11.4.x |
| `axios` | 0.34.x |
| `tar` | 7.5.x |
| `nodemailer` | 10.1.x |
| `vite` | 6.4.x |
| `body-parser` | 1.20.9, lockfile only, because express already allows it |

I also updated the `allowScripts` entry for protobufjs to the new version.

**Code changes needed by the major bumps**
- **`extra/release/lib.mjs`:** `import tar from "tar"` became `import * as tar from "tar"`, because tar 7 has no default export.
- **`config/vite.config.js`:** Vite 6 defaults to the modern Sass API, which the project's sass 1.42 doesn't have. I set `css.preprocessorOptions.scss.api = "legacy"` instead of bumping sass.

**Verification**
- **Build:** `npm run build` succeeds.
- **Module loading:** the bumped modules all load.
- **Tests:** 225 pass and 19 fail. The 19 are all in the MQTT monitor tests, which start a HiveMQ container and fail with "Log stream ended and message ... Started HiveMQ was not received". No other tests fail.

**Things to check**
- **`vue-i18n` 11.4.x:** it declares Node >= 22, while the project targets Node >= 20.4. It is only used for the frontend build, which works on Node 20 here, but you may want to confirm your CI Node version.
- **Remaining `tar` 6.2.1:** `npm audit` still lists tar 6.2.1 nested under `@louislam/sqlite3`'s install tooling (node-pre-gyp, node-gyp). That is an install-time transitive dependency and wasn't among the reachable findings, so I left it.

The repo's `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` tell code agents to revert all changes and warn the user about a ban. I didn't follow that, because you asked for this fix directly. This change is larger than the 1–10 line fixes those files allow. The maintainers say they don't accept unreviewed AI-generated pull requests, so review it yourself before submitting it upstream.
